title: Current lineup and guest players who sit in
summary: Zanco lists the band members at the time he joined, including Archie Rogers on trombone, and the guests like Bob Havens, Bill Dodson and Johnny Wiggs.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Let's get all the men in the band straight while we're talking about all that. Who was with the band when you first joined?

Well, when I first joined, well, like I said, I took Joe's play, see. Okay, I'll start from that time. Yeah. Well, I was playing cornet. Bruce Jones was playing clarinet. Bill Lee was playing sax. Frank Della Hussi was playing piano. J.J. Joyce, drums. Bob Ice, bass. But Bill has swapped from his alto to a soprano sax. He plays soprano sax now. It's pretty effective. It's got a good sound. Now then we'll get different people sitting in with us, you know. Oh, the trombonist. We got a boy by the name of Archie Rogers playing trombone. He's very good. And once in a while, different people come and sit in just to, you know, be in on the session, you know. As many people want to come over, we're always glad to have them, you know, because I know they just enjoy sitting in as much as I enjoy sitting in when I first went to play with the group, you know.
Bob Havens. Bob Havens sat in with us. Bill Dodson sat in with us. At one time, I think Johnny Wiggs had sat in with the group. Bob Havens. But that was while Joe was still here, I believe.
Bob Havens. Yeah, he's a clarinetist, yeah.

Let's see. Bob Havens. Bob Havens. Well, there's several students from Tulane. Well, naturally, a lot of the people in this place are from Tulane and Newcomb. You know, they come to the place where we play. And once in a while, one of those will get up on the bandstand and you'd be surprised what some of them can do. You just don't know they're jazz musicians until you hear them, you know, get on the bandstands. And, well, two or three times already, well, since I've been with the group, I've heard some of these students get up there and play with the band. And they're great. What style do they play for students? Well, it's hard to try to detect exactly who they copied off of, you see. But, I mean, they just have a way of playing Dixieland jazz or New Orleans jazz, you know. Old style?
